title: Al-Muhalla bi al-Athar
author: ibn-hazm
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: The great law book of the Zahiri school. Ibn Hazm numbers each question, states his ruling from the plain sense of the Qur'an and hadith, and then reviews and rejects the positions of the other schools, refusing analogy and juristic preference as sources.
historicalContext: Ibn Hazm of Cordoba was a poet, historian and theologian as well as a jurist. The Muhalla, left unfinished and completed by his son, is the fullest surviving statement of literalist law and a rich record of the opinions of the early jurists.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
